transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-08-14
- Start: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Ava Liu (Redwood CSM); Mike Alvarez (CTO, Orison); Leah Kim (SRE); Dr. Sam Bennett (ML Eng); Carlos Vega (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Redwood presented week-3 POC bench contrasts vs customer incumbent; main wins on P50 latency and median throughput, some P95 spikes with long-tail tokens, discussed routing decisions, KV/prefix cache, and quantization trade-offs. Agreed to run another side-by-side with tightened batch and with KMS-encrypted cache to mirror customer constraints. Next steps and owners listed.

Topics:
- Quick recap of last week's tuning
- Bench numbers: p50/p95 latency, sustained throughput, unit cost delta vs incumbent
- Root cause of P95 spikes (prefix size, network jitter, fallback routing)
- Quantization artifacts and quality checks
- Security constraints (KMS, SOC2 logs, VPC egress)
- Action plan and pilot next sprint

Transcript body:
[00:00:05] Jordan Park: okay thanks everyone for jumping on, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, um Priya will run through the numbers and i will add commercial context at the end.
[00:00:15] Priya Nair: hi all, yeah i pulled the week three run, so we did 24 hours of steady-state plus three 20 minute bursts simulating your daytime traffic. baseline here is your incumbent, IncumbentAI, which you shared last week. quick note: some labels in the logs got munged — we saw "Redwood Optima" in a few rows, that's our Redwood Optimize hints, not a different product.
[00:00:45] Mike Alvarez: yeah cool, and thanks again for keeping those runs aligned. one ask up front — can you remind us if the KV cache was enabled in these runs? we had concerns about prefix cache size and the SRE team wants parity with our live cache config.
[00:00:58] Priya Nair: good call — for the default run KV cache was enabled but with our conservative 64MB prefix cap to match your mem limits. we also did a run with cache off, and a run with cache at 256MB. results below.
[00:01:20] Dr. Sam Bennett: clarify — when you say cached, is it full prefix caching or is it the K V saved token cache? sometimes transcripts show K V cash and i get confused.
[00:01:28] Priya Nair: sorry yes that's the KV (key-value) autokv cache — token level prefix caching.
[00:01:35] Leah Kim: we also have strict egress rules; if the cache is encrypted with customer KMS we need to know CPU overhead for decryption.
[00:01:44] Priya Nair: noted — we did an encrypted-kms trial in the separate run. overhead was ~3-5% on latency P50. we'll share the trace.

[00:02:20] Priya Nair: now the numbers: P50 latency — Redwood: 42ms; IncumbentAI: 68ms. P95 latency — Redwood: 248ms; IncumbentAI: 310ms. sustained throughput (tokens/sec) — Redwood: 4,500 t/s; IncumbentAI: 3,200 t/s. unit-token cost (approx) — Redwood: $0.0009/token vs IncumbentAI: $0.0013/token given your batch profile. these are median runs across three repeats.
[00:02:56] Carlos Vega: whoa that P50 is nice, but the P95 for both is pretty high. what's accounting for the P95 spikes on the Redwood side?
[00:03:05] Priya Nair: good question — we profiled and found two main contributors: 1) long or unusual prompts causing retracing of KV cache paths, and 2) fallback routing when a dedicated slot briefly saturated and traffic spilled to lower-tier nodes. we did see a spike when a background cuda memcpy overlapped with small-batch inference on one GPU.
[00:03:30] Jordan Park: to add, some of the P95 tail is network jitter between your VPC and our private egress point in us-east-1; in the hosted run we saw more consistent latency because traffic is in-region. once we mirror your VPC egress with our private deployment the tail should tighten.
[00:03:48] Leah Kim: ok but on encryption — that KMS decryption overhead, is that per-token or per-request? because if it's per-request it's less bad for us.
[00:03:56] Priya Nair: it's per-request; we decrypt per-session/handle not per token, so overhead is mostly fixed and amortized across longer responses.

[00:04:25] Dr. Sam Bennett: about quantization — last week you ran int8, any quality regressions? we care about hallucination rates on our medical rewrite prompts.
[00:04:33] Priya Nair: for int8 with calibration we saw negligible quality delta on top-100 eval prompts, but on a small subset of rare tokens post-200 sequence you see some variance. we recommended int8+fused at batch=4 for your workload profile.
[00:04:52] Mike Alvarez: can you show a quick chart of throughput vs batch? i think that was the last slide.
[00:05:00] Priya Nair: sure — we measured batch=1,2,4,8. throughput: batch1 1800 t/s, batch2 3000 t/s, batch4 4500 t/s, batch8 5200 t/s but latency rises as expected. for your 95th percentile SLA we think batch4 is the sweet spot.
[00:05:24] Jordan Park: also note cost trade — batch8 reduces unit cost but increased p95 by ~40%. for latency-sensitive routes we recommend batch4 with prefix caching.

[00:06:10] Leah Kim: on routing — you mentioned fallback to lower-tier nodes; can we pin certain high-priority routes to dedicated slots so there's no spill? our legal team requires deterministic latency for certain features.
[00:06:20] Jordan Park: yes you can pin routes to dedicated capacity; we can reserve dedicated slots for that feature and configure autoscale thresholds to avoid spill. there's a cost delta that we'll include in the commercial delta sheet.

[00:06:45] Priya Nair: quick demo: here's an example trace where a route was pinned but we had a transient IO stall — you can see the trace id 0x7f3a where the kernel preemption caused a 70ms tail. couple mitigations: 1) HA pairing of slots, 2) fine-grained preemption windows, 3) avoid live snapshot backups during peak windows.
[00:07:15] Mike Alvarez: are those mitigations automatic or do they need ops changes?
[00:07:20] Priya Nair: HA pairing and preemption windows are config level and we can enable them for your dedicated pool; backups scheduling is on your side but we can recommend blackout windows.

[00:07:50] Carlos Vega: any regressions vs your earlier run last month? I remember you had a large improvement after kernel tune.
[00:07:55] Priya Nair: compared to July's run we improved P50 by ~12ms thanks to kernel selection tweaks and improved batching heuristics; P95 improved slightly only when cache hit-rate exceeded 82%. when hit-rate drops below that you see tail drift.

[00:08:30] Dr. Sam Bennett: what about model variants? you said Redwood can fallback to a smaller quantized model — what is the expected latency delta and quality delta?
[00:08:40] Priya Nair: fallback to smaller quantized model lowers P50 to ~28ms but reduces throughput per-GPU slightly; quality delta is model-specific — on your eval set we saw a 1.8% BLEU-like score drop on structured extraction tasks; for free-form generation the delta was less pronounced.

[00:09:05] Leah Kim: let's talk security checklist briefly — SOC2 scope, SAML/SSO, audit logs with token-level telemetry, and key management. do you have SOC2 reports and can you provide a data flow diagram?
[00:09:15] Jordan Park: yes SOC2 report available; and we can provide a VPC data flow diagram. SAML is supported; token-level telemetry exported to your SIEM is also supported with log retention options. we'll drop the security pack link after the call.

[00:09:50] Mike Alvarez: one of our engineers asked about deterministic E2E latency for a demo next month — can you guarantee a P95 under 200ms for a 16-turn dialogue scenario?
[00:10:00] Jordan Park: not via hosted baseline but with dedicated slots, KV cache warm, and pinned routing in us-east-1, we think a P95 under 200ms is achievable for typical dialogs. we'll validate with the side-by-side run.

[00:10:28] Priya Nair: switching back to bench details — i want to call out an anomalous run we saw at 02:14 UTC where a pod OOM caused a cascade; that increased P95 to ~420ms for 6 minutes. root cause there was an out-of-bound prompt length causing cache bloat, we patched a hard cap in the allocator.
[00:10:50] Leah Kim: good, please annotate that run in the shared sheet so we can track flaky ones.

[00:11:15] Jordan Park: quick commercial note — on Dedicated pricing we can offer a trial 2-week reserved window with reduced commit to validate in production; will follow-up with the delta sheet.
[00:11:25] Mike Alvarez: what about the incurrent vendor price — how deep is the unit delta?
[00:11:30] Jordan Park: based on the week's runs and your token mix, unit cost delta is roughly 25% savings with our default config; with quantization and higher batch you can push to 35-40% but it's a quality/cost trade.

[00:11:55] Carlos Vega: are there any features the incumbent has that you can't match? e.g., inline reranking or a specific API for streaming?
[00:12:02] Priya Nair: we support streaming and function/tool calling; inline reranking we do as a separate rerank step in the pipeline — if you need single-call rerank we'll build a custom route but it may add a small latency penalty.

[00:12:28] Dr. Sam Bennett: ok let's plan the side-by-side: can Redwood run with identical input and encryption settings? especially KMS and VPC egress.
[00:12:36] Priya Nair: yes we can mirror encryption and egress; we will need your KMS public key and a temporary IAM role to mount the test bucket.

[00:12:55] Mike Alvarez: timeline — we want verification before the demo on Sept 2. is that realistic?
[00:13:00] Jordan Park: yes, if we get the traces and keys this week we can schedule the run for week of Aug 24 and deliver an analysis by Aug 27, which leaves time for the dry run before Sept 2.

[00:13:25] Leah Kim: a nit — your trace ids in the spreadsheet are truncated sometimes, please give full trace links.
[00:13:31] Priya Nair: will do, sorry about that.

[00:14:05] Jordan Park: quick callout on observability — Redwood Console will expose token-level costs, model-level latency breakdowns, and route traces. we can onboard your SREs for a walkthrough.
[00:14:20] Carlos Vega: yes please include our SRE in that onboarding.

[00:14:40] Priya Nair: ok last technical point — we spotted a small discrepancy between our local perf harness and your production trace: your production uses slightly different tokenizer (we saw 2 tokens difference on avg) which affects token counts. we'll normalize tokenization in the next run.
[00:15:05] Dr. Sam Bennett: good to hear.

[00:15:30] Jordan Park: let's surface explicit next steps now so it's clear.
[00:15:35] Priya Nair: agreed. (lists) 1) Redwood: share full bench spreadsheet + annotated anomalies. 2) Redwood: updated routing playbook and commitment sheet. 3) Orison: provide KMS public key + IAM role + 24h production traces. 4) Orison SRE to join Redwood Console onboarding.
[00:16:05] Mike Alvarez: makes sense. any blockers from Redwood side?
[00:16:10] Jordan Park: just access to the key artifacts; also we'll need a short MOU for the dedicated trial — we can draft and send.

[00:16:40] Carlos Vega: one last question — during the encrypted-kms run did you see CPU steal on the host from KMS agent?
[00:16:48] Priya Nair: negligible, <2% CPU but we saw 3-5% added latency P50 as mentioned earlier, mostly in tiny requests.

[00:17:05] Leah Kim: okay thanks. i'm a bit worried about the P95 tails still but the plan to pin routes and do a side-by-side should help.
[00:17:15] Jordan Park: understood. we'll prioritize the side-by-side with pinned routes.

[00:17:30] Ava Liu: quick note — i'll follow up with a checklist and the security pack links after the call.
[00:17:40] Mike Alvarez: great, thanks everyone.

Closing recap (auto):
- Redwood shows leading P50 latency and higher throughput in baseline tests.
- P95 tails exist due to cache hit-rate variance, fallback routing, and occasional host-level stalls.
- Agreed mitigations: pin high-priority routes to dedicated slots, enable HA pairing, normalize tokenizer, run side-by-side with KMS-encrypted cache and VPC egress parity.
- Owners assigned for bench reruns, artifact uploads, and commercial sheet.

End of transcript.
